text.p: Guinea's president, Lansana Conte, has shuffled his government, naming Ibrahima Kosory Fofana as minister delegate for finance and economic planning.

A presidential decree published on Friday said that Fofana, former minister delegate for budget and privatisation, and Ousmane Kaba, former minister delegate for finance and the economy, would switch jobs.
Political sources said Fofana was from Conte's Susu tribe and that the switch was a sign of support for Fofana following rivalry with Kaba over who was responsible for what.
Conte, an army general who seized power in 1985, won disputed elections in 1993.

He appointed Prime Minister Sidia Toure, a technocrat and businessman who once worked in Ivory Coast, in July 1996 to restore confidence after a bloody army revolt over pay shook the country the previous Febuary.
Sidia Toure holds the main finance and planning portfolio.
